channel.title: doyouknow.app - English
channel.description: Surprising facts about UAE, Saudi Arabia, and the world.

item.title: How Egypt's Real Estate Registration System Works
item.description: Egypt's official property registration system protects buyers from fraud in ways a simple sale contract cannot. Here is how it actually works.

item.title: How Saudi Arabia's New Rail Lines Are Actually Being Built
item.description: Saudi Arabia is expanding its rail network fast. Here is how desert rail lines get engineered, funded, and connected to ports and cities.

item.title: How Sports Medals Are Actually Made
item.description: How Olympic-style gold, silver, and bronze medals are actually designed, minted, and secured, including why a 'gold' medal is mostly silver underneath.

item.title: How Streaming Recommendation Algorithms Actually Work
item.description: How streaming recommendations actually work: collaborative filtering, the cold-start problem, why watch time drives everything, and why guesses are sometimes eerily right.

item.title: How Saudi Arabia's Elm Platform Handles Government Services
item.description: Elm is a public-private technology company behind many Saudi digital services, distinct from Absher. Here is how it actually works.

item.title: How a 'Record' Heat Wave Actually Gets Verified
item.description: A record-breaking temperature claim isn't official until it survives a slow, methodical verification process. Here's how that process works.

item.title: Why Children's Product Recalls Happen So Often
item.description: Why toys and baby gear get recalled far more often than adult products: stricter safety thresholds, how recalls actually get triggered, and what parents should check.

item.title: Why Clock Changes Don't Happen on the Same Date Everywhere
item.description: Why daylight saving transitions fall on different dates in different countries, why some places skip the change entirely, and the scheduling chaos this creates.

item.title: Why Cricket Bowlers Get Called for 'Throwing' the Ball
item.description: Cricket bowlers get called for 'throwing' when their elbow bends too much mid-action. Here's the biomechanics rule and how it's actually tested.

item.title: Why Deepfake Detection Keeps Losing to Deepfake Creation
item.description: Deepfake detectors are structurally always a step behind generators. Here's why the arms race is so lopsided and what actually helps.

item.title: Why Doomscrolling Is So Hard to Stop, Even When It Feels Bad
item.description: Doomscrolling isn't a willpower failure. It's a predictable response to how feeds are built and how attention actually works.

item.title: Why Exam Halls Follow Such Strict, Almost Ritualistic Rules
item.description: The history behind exam-hall rules: seating spacing, timing precision, sealed papers, and why each requirement traces back to a real, documented cheating method.

item.title: Why Extreme Heat Kills More People Than Extreme Cold
item.description: Heat overwhelms the body's cooling system faster than cold overwhelms its warming system. Here's the physiology behind the deadlier extreme.

item.title: Why Flight Prices Seem to Rise the Moment You Search Twice
item.description: Airline pricing explained: why fares change between searches, why clearing cookies sometimes seems to work, and what actually moves the number you see.

item.title: Why Gulf Humidity Feels Worse Than the Thermometer Says
item.description: Why a Gulf summer day can feel far hotter than the reported temperature: the science of heat index, wet-bulb temperature, and why coastal humidity is different from desert heat.

item.title: Why Moon Sighting Still Matters for Setting Islamic Dates
item.description: Why Islamic months still start with observing the crescent moon rather than a fixed calendar, and why different countries sometimes announce different dates for the same occasion.

item.title: Why Movie Premieres Still Matter in the Streaming Era
item.description: Movie premieres still happen even when films stream days later. Here's the marketing and economic logic that keeps the red carpet alive.

item.title: Why Rumors About Public Figures Spread Faster Than the Facts
item.description: The psychology and platform mechanics that let an unverified claim about a public figure outrun its correction, and how to read the next viral claim more carefully.

item.title: Why Sports Drinks Contain More Sugar Than People Realize
item.description: Sports drinks carry more sugar than most people expect. Here's the science behind why, and when water actually works better.

item.title: Why the 2026 World Cup Expanded to 48 Teams
item.description: The 2026 World Cup is the first with 48 teams instead of 32. Here is why FIFA expanded it and what actually changes on the pitch.
